hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK, tolerating approximately -20 to -15°C.
visual: Cascading silver-grey foliage · creamy-white spring blossom · elegant weeping crown
water: Water regularly during establishment. Once established, tolerates moderately dry conditions.
prune: Prune lightly in winter to remove damaged, crossing or unwanted shoots. Preserve the natural weeping shape.
toxicity: The small ornamental fruits should not be eaten by people or pets. Some branches may have sharp thorns, so wear gloves when handling.
resilience: Tolerates wind, urban conditions and some drought once established. May suffer from aphids, pear rust, scab or fireblight.
uses: Specimen tree · small gardens · silver foliage contrast · Mediterranean-style planting · coastal gardens
foliage: deciduous; narrow, willow-like leaves covered in fine silvery-grey hairs
pollination: not applicable; grown ornamentally rather than for an edible fruit crop
uncertain: Height and spread vary between authoritative sources. RHS cultivar profile lists 8-12 m tall and over 8 m wide, while RHS garden guidance and specialist tree nurseries describe approximately 5-6 m. The latter is used as a typical landscape size, not an absolute maximum.
Pest risk, thirst, care level, growth speed and sun requirement are horticultural estimates on the Timber scales.
No reliable cultivar-specific root depth and spread measurements established.
The minimum tolerated sunlight threshold has not been quantified.

hardinessNote: Hardy throughout the UK, tolerating approximately -20 to -15°C.
visual: Fiery orange-red spring leaves · golden summer foliage · clusters of deep pink flowers
soilWarning: Foliage colour fades in excessive shade
water: Water regularly during establishment and prolonged dry spells. Mulch in spring to conserve moisture.
prune: Cut stems back to approximately 15 cm above ground in early spring to encourage vigorous, brightly coloured new growth. Deadhead after flowering.
cvs: 'Gold Mound' – bright golden foliage · 'Golden Princess' – compact golden leaves · 'Firelight' – vivid orange-red young growth
resilience: Hardy, adaptable and generally pest-free. Tolerates urban conditions and a range of soil types. Occasionally susceptible to honey fungus.
uses: Front of borders · low hedging · mass planting · patio containers · wildlife gardens · foliage contrast
foliage: deciduous; oval leaves emerge orange-red, mature through yellow and gold to green, with warm autumn tones
uncertain: Also listed under the synonyms Spiraea × bumalda 'Gold Flame' and Spiraea × bumalda 'Goldflame'; RHS accepts Spiraea japonica 'Goldflame'.
Sunlight, pest risk, water demand, maintenance and growth-speed scores are horticultural estimates rather than published measurements.
SunMin is an estimated shade-tolerance threshold based on RHS acceptance of partial shade.
Flowering usually peaks in midsummer. The broader Apr-Sep display period includes ornamental foliage.
No reliable cultivar-specific root depth and spread measurements established.
